summary: vectormark ships remote-code-fetch sink disguised as an Avalanche RPC endpoint
details: The package advertises itself as a zero-dependency SVG helper but exports an undocumented getPlugin() that issues an HTTPS GET to the hardcoded lookalike host api.avax-test.dev (typosquat of the legitimate Avalanche Fuji host api.avax-test.network) with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false), then passes the response body to new Function('require', data)(require). Any caller reaching getPlugin() executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the installer's Node process with full require access. The endpoint is variable-named AVALANCHE_FUJI_RPC_URL and referenced alongside SNOWTRACE_API_KEY to resemble blockchain RPC plumbing, but the response body is treated as executable code, not JSON-RPC data. README does not mention getPlugin or any network behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
